quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic movement. They are white with black markings. You must always obey them.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. A green arrow means:

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means go, like a green light. But you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may proceed only if the green arrow is with a circular green light.
It points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means go, like a green light. But you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means the same as a circular green light. But traffic in that lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: Your accelerator sticks while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral quickly. Press the brake firmly. Pull off the road when safe and turn off the engine.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Emotions affect your driving. If you are worried, excited, scared, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress makes it hard to focus on driving. It is better to wait and drive when you feel stable.

questions.question: When you approach an uncontrolled intersection, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop, look in all directions, and go.

questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or traffic signal, yield to cars coming from the right. Always be ready to yield to avoid a crash. Do this by easing off the gas, covering the brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive the same way you do on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. Your car will take longer to stop than it does on normal roads.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
Together, they can strengthen the effects of both.
They have no effect because they are different.

questions.correctAnswerText: Together, they can strengthen the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other drugs can increase how much both affect you. For example, one drink with cold medicine could affect you as much as several drinks alone.

questions.question: You see a railroad crossing with a standard crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Approach carefully and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for a train.
Only go when a flagger tells you it is safe.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings carefully. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: When you see an accident scene, you should:

options.text: Stop if you are involved or if emergency help is not there yet.

questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to accidents just to look.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying full attention to driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: You must use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane. Why?

options.text: The person is a police officer.

questions.explanation: A white cane means a person is blind. When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop. This keeps them safe.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it mean on a sign?

options.text: Some drivers must yield to others.
Drive slower than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means no. These signs are white rectangles with red and black marks. The red circle and slash over a symbol means that action is forbidden.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the road shoulder and empty.
When it comes toward you, even without flashing lights.
On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic from both directions must stop. The bus will have red lights flashing at the top and a stop arm on the left side.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?
questions.explanation: Slow down when it rains, snows, or sleets. These conditions make roads slippery. You may need to drive slower than the posted speed limit to stay safe.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You can pass, even if it is dangerous.
You can pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. A dashed white line means you can cross it to pass or change lanes, but only if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They need the same space as cars to turn.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the back. Do not stay in these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than cars do.

questions.question: You find a problem with your vehicle that could affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have the money.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any problem that could affect safe driving must be fixed right away. Do not drive the vehicle until it is fixed.

questions.question: A driver on an entrance ramp joining a highway should:

options.text: Let drivers already on the highway go first.
Expect other drivers to move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let drivers already on the highway go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a highway from an entrance or acceleration ramp, yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when there is a gap in traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.
A divided highway starts. Slow to the safe speed shown.
Merge into traffic. Slow to the safe speed shown.
Winding road ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the road curves to the right. Slow down to the safe speed listed on the sign (in this case, 35 mph).

questions.question: What do orange signs mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn of work zones on the road. These signs are diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers that workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill next to a curb, turn your steering wheel away from the curb and set the parking brake. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: The main reason drinking alcohol and driving is dangerous is that it affects your:
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your blood and reaches your brain in 20 to 40 minutes. It damages the parts of your brain that control judgment and skill.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in driveways with the engine running.

questions.explanation: Quick stops waste fuel because you use fuel to speed back up. Drivers who look ahead can slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid hard braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The left lane is reserved for vehicles with a specific number of occupants.
Specific turning movements are allowed from specific lanes.
Drivers in both lanes are responsible for merging smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is reserved for vehicles with a specific number of occupants.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. These lanes are reserved for buses and cars with a driver plus one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while driving. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you need more effort to steer. Slow down and carefully drive to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: Distracted drivers are at greater risk of a crash when using which of the following?
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player while driving is distracting and increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
Drivers consistently checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers maintaining a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for road conditions. Always obey speed limits and drive slower when conditions are poor.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, you should:
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, sound your horn if you think another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and how fast oncoming traffic is moving.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line in the middle. What does this tell you?

options.text: Traffic moves in both directions on this road.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in both directions on this road.
questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you may cross it to pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: To avoid sudden braking or turning, how far ahead should you look while driving?
questions.explanation: Look at least 10 seconds ahead of your vehicle to avoid sudden stops or lane changes. This gives you time to react safely and helps traffic flow smoothly.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow line to pass another car?

options.text: Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the car ahead is going slower than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean neither direction of traffic may cross them. You can only cross them to turn into a driveway or business entrance. Passing is never allowed across a solid yellow line.
